title: Planar lineage tags the records imply but do not state
summary: The library carried nine tanar'ri and eight baatezu and no demons or devils, ten celestials filed only as archons, angels, guardinals and eladrin, and twenty-odd fiends that never said `fiend`. None of that is wrong — it is what the source calls them — but a tag is a filter, and a filter nobody knows to type is not one. scripts/srd/tag-taxonomy.mjs states the entailments (`baatezu` -> `devil` -> `fiend`, `tanar-ri` -> `demon` -> `fiend`, `archon`/`angel`/`guardinal`/`eladrin` -> `celestial`, `chromatic` -> `dragon` + `evil`) and this repair writes them onto the records that already state the specific half. The specific tags stay: a consumer that wants baatezu only can still have them. One record also drops `true`, which meant 'a true dragon' beside a `dragon` tag that already said it. Every repair here sets `tags` and nothing else, so no rating, encounter field or mechanic moves and no approved decision is invalidated — the ledger hashes the base record, which this does not touch.

repairs.rationale: Tags only. The controlled vocabulary in scripts/srd/tag-taxonomy.mjs entails broader lineage tags from the specific ones this record already states, and the record shipped the specific tag without the umbrella: `celestial` because the source names the order — archon, angel, guardinal, eladrin — and never the family they all belong to. Nothing mechanical changes.
